A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CoVoGAN and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices. Retained material can be matched reliably across the reformatting, renumbering and additions.

before.justification: v2 reports original video-generation, disentanglement, ablation and computational-efficiency results in Tables 1–3 and 6, alongside generated-video examples.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds dataset evaluations, supervised diffusion adaptations, longer-video results and latent-variable analyses.

M1.justification: v3 adds TTM adaptations that condition Wan-1.3B and MotionCtrl through cross-attention (Appendix F.3), extending the procedure beyond its original GAN implementation. The core CoVoGAN architecture and losses remain. Equation 5 also changes the GRU noise-input index from t to t−1, without explaining whether this reflects an implementation change or a correction.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained FaceForensics, SkyTimelapse and RealEstate coverage, v3 evaluates CelebV-HQ celebrity faces and TaiChi human motion. It also adds WebVid-10M text-conditioned generation and camera-trajectory-conditioned generation on RealEstate10K, substantially expanding the represented populations and task requirements.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds LVDM and Latte to the disentanglement comparison, from which v2 explicitly excluded diffusion models. New Tables 8–9 evaluate against Wan-1.3B, CogVideoX-2B and MotionCtrl. Comparator membership for the original Table 1 datasets remains unchanged.

E3.justification: v3 introduces 128-dimensional PCA representations for diffusion disentanglement evaluation, 32-frame FaceForensics testing, and new resolution settings for CelebV-HQ and TaiChi. Appendix F.3 adds Wan fine-tuning on the first 10% of WebVid-10M and evaluations using VBench, CLIP similarities, CamMC and FID. These are new protocols, not evidence that the retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The original GRU/flow ablations remain unchanged. v3 adds tests of longer-video generation, sensitivity to motion-latent dimensionality, and independent recombination of content and motion variables (Tables 6, 7 and 12). These substantially broaden the diagnostic questions beyond removing individual architectural components.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. Removing v2's checklist also removes its computational-cost explanation for omitting error bars, but the statistical reporting practice remains unchanged.

E6.justification: Original entries in Tables 1–3 and the efficiency results, moved from Table 6 to Table 10, are unchanged. v3 adds substantial results, including CoVoGAN FVD16 of 97.16 on CelebV-HQ and FVD of 55.3 on TaiChi. New Table 8 reports mixed TTM+Wan/Wan outcomes: subject consistency is 0.9529/0.9324, while aesthetic quality is 0.4924/0.5370. These are newly reported comparisons, not same-setting gains over v2.

T1.justification: The identifiability definitions, theorem assumptions and Appendix A.1 proofs are retained. New Appendix A.3 adds mathematical cases and stated conditions for operator injectivity, including an additive-noise Fourier condition and invertible transformations. This is a limited theoretical supplement, without a new identifiability theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and four principal contributions retain the same claims about TTM, CoVoGAN, block-wise/component-wise identifiability and improved generation and control. The added experiments support these retained claims without redefining the main contribution.

C2.justification: v3 explains that oversized motion latents may fit noise and undersized ones may merge factors (F.2). It explicitly qualifies the diffusion adaptations as not fully aligned with the theoretical framework (F.3), explains missing TaiChi metrics through keypoint-extraction failure, and shifts the conclusion's future-work emphasis from text-to-video integration toward open-domain applications.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies the 2,368 SkyTimelapse videos, explains metric computation in Appendix D, and identifies evaluation tools and adaptation details such as MediaPipe, CLIP implementations and the WebVid subset. The original hardware, convergence budget and configuration Tables 4–5 remain unchanged. Both versions state that code is supplied in supplementary materials.

R1.justification: The existing related-work discussion and novelty positioning largely persist. v3 adds targeted references for the new datasets, metrics and operator examples, and connects its cross-attention adaptation to Xie et al.'s identifiable image-generation work. The switch to author–year citations is formatting rather than a change in research positioning.

P1.justification: Most core prose and the main section order are retained. v3 consolidates identifiability explanations into Section 2.3, adds a roadmap and metric-details appendix, shortens experimental exposition, and removes the NeurIPS checklist while adding a reproducibility statement. These are localized narrative and structural revisions rather than a wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: v3 substantially changes the template and evidence displays: Tables 1–2 gain columns, several tables wrap within text and highlight CoVoGAN entries, and six new tables and Figures 8–9 are added. Existing figures are resized or relocated, while Figure 5 retains its examples with revised labels and caption. The efficiency table is retained as Table 10.

improvement.justification: Adding diffusion baselines to Table 2 and testing latent-size sensitivity and independent recombination gives the central disentanglement claims more direct empirical scrutiny. Broader domains also strengthen the evaluation. The net gain is limited by sparse integration and training-control details for the diffusion adaptations, their acknowledged mismatch with the theory, and Table 12's omission of the FVD evidence claimed in its text. Uncertainty estimates remain absent.
